Technical priorities: VPC private control plane, audit log streaming to Splunk (TLS), long retention (7 years) for audit logs, cross-account IAM roles for Redwood control plane, support for SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, S3 interface via VPC endpoints for model artifact pulls, egress minimized and via NAT+VPC endpoints.

Latency/throughput targets: p95 < 150ms for chat flows (short context), sustained 500 req/s for embeddings/reranking bursts. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for Dedicated/Private if ROI on SLAs clear.

Model preferences: open models preferred (quantized versions ok) but must support deterministic rollback to a pinned model version. Need automatic fallback policy to smaller model when capacity constrained.

Security review status: Initial security questionnaire returned (see drive doc). Next is architecture review with network team and KMS key custody legal review.

architecture_fit_summary: Prefer single-tenant VPC per account with private control plane. Proposed topology: customer-managed VPC with dedicated subnets for inference nodes, private endpoints for S3/Glue/Secrets Manager, no public NAT for control plane traffic; outbound-only to Redwood management plane via enforced proxy or PrivateLink. Option A: VPC Peering to Redwood transit VPC for low-latency path (simple but scales less). Option B: Transit Gateway + shared services for multi-region customers (recommended for >3 VPCs). KMS model: BYOK using AWS CloudHSM + cross-account grants to Redwood service principal; fallback option Redwood-managed KMS with strict key policy. Audit logs: push to customer-owned S3 + Kinesis Firehose to Splunk; ensure encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS keys. Region strategy: primary us-east-1, DR/replica in eu-west-1 (for EMEA customers), model artifacts must be region-bound unless explicit replication signed off by legal.
